items.title: Millionaire economist's dire warning for Australian property market
items.description: British economist Gary Stevenson is on a speaking tour, warning Australia will follow the path of the UK with "poverty exploding" unless politicians deal with inequality.

items.title: Land prices have risen by more than 500 per cent since 2000
items.description: A Housing Industry Association report says rising land prices are blocking the construction of new homes.

items.title: Hanson issues partial apology for suggestion there are no 'good' Muslims
items.description: The One Nation leader qualified her earlier remarks, which had been met with condemnation, while reiterating calls for tougher vetting processes for Muslim migrants.

items.title: Long-time Bupa customer left $30k out of pocket after shoulder replacement denied
items.description: Australians are increasingly downgrading their health cover, with 360,000 people leaving gold policies since 2020. But some have been left out of pocket for surgeries they thought they were covered for.

items.title: Australia 'must allow' IS-linked families to return, UN expert says
items.description: Australian families with links to Islamic State fighters should be returned to Australia to prevent harm and potential radicalisation of innocent children, according to United Nations special rapporteur Ben Saul.

items.title: A dead teenager, a TikTok brag track and a parent's dismissal of gang activity
items.description: Ater "Elia" Good was gunned down early this year, with police alleging it was a gang-related killing. His parents say their son was not a gang member but are aware activity is on the rise.

items.title: Prison conditions for Netflix star Matt Wright revealed
items.description: Matt Wright, the star of Netflix's Outback Wrangler, has been separated from the general prison population at the Darwin Correctional Centre, where most inmates contend with overcrowding and extreme heat.

items.title: The engineer trying to stop NASA's Artemis II launch going around the Moon
items.description: After years of delays, NASA's Artemis II mission is aiming to launch next month. But issues with the heat shield are causing some to raise the alarm.

items.title: HungryPanda delivery drivers say police contacted family back home
items.description: Riders embroiled in a dispute over pay and conditions with food delivery company HungryPanda in Sydney say Chinese police have asserted pressure back home to stop them protesting.

items.title: Live: One Nation expecting a 'Melbourne Cup'-like race to decide Farrer candidate
items.description: One Nation leader Pauline Hanson says about 80 people have applied to be the party's candidate for Farrer in the upcoming by-election. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Health insurers surge ahead of premium hike, ASX rises
items.description: Shares of health insurers have surged ahead of premium hikes while the ASX has started its day higher, and NAB has reported a 30 per cent jump in quarterly profit. Follow live.

items.title: Iran announces closure of vital shipping route during US nuclear talks
items.description: Iran says it temporarily closed the Strait of Hormuz — a vital international shipping route — as it entered a new round of talks with the US over its nuclear capabilities.

items.title: Retelling the story of a bridge that 'tore a nation of people apart'
items.description: In the 1990s, a group of Indigenous women were accused of fabricating claims of sacred sites to stop the construction of a bridge south of Adelaide. It was a decision that has impacted a community for decades.

items.title: One bold investment in an empty building transformed this country town's main street
items.description: A few years ago, Charleville's main street had lost its spark, with storefronts empty and windows shuttered. So, what does it take to bring a main street back to life?

items.title: One man dead, another in serious condition after Bruce Highway crash
items.description: One man has died and another is in a life-threatening condition after a truck crashed into a car while driving the wrong direction on the Bruce Highway on Tuesday night.

items.title: Shia LaBeouf arrested for allegedly hitting two men at Mardi Gras in New Orleans
items.description: The actor allegedly hit a man multiple times with closed fists and allegedly punched another man in the nose.

items.title: OCD is often misunderstood. How much do you really know about it?
items.description: Elena wants people with OCD to know they're not alone. But how well do Australians understand the condition?

items.title: Civil rights leader Jesse Jackson dies, aged 84
items.description: The two-time Democratic presidential hopeful remembered for powerful speeches died peacefully surrounded by loved ones, his family said.

items.title: Man who escaped mental health care facility fronts court over Sydney stabbings
items.description: A 25-year-old man police say stabbed a man to death in Merrylands days after fleeing from health authorities has been charged with murder.

items.title: Randa Abdel-Fattah to feature at Sydney Writers' Festival
items.description: Sydney Writers' Festival has defended featuring Randa Abdel-Fattah on its 2026 program, saying it is "not in the business of cancelling or censoring writers".

items.title: Track closure will see 'flood' of greyhounds needing new homes
items.description: One hundred years of greyhound racing in far west NSW is about to come to an end.

items.title: Fire threat eases but central Victorian blaze still out of control
items.description: Authorities say weather conditions have helped fire crews battling a blaze that threatened homes near Trawool, south of Seymour.

items.title: Police to return to Oak Park 'frequently' in search for Gus Lamont
items.description: SA's Police Commissioner says officers will be returning to Oak Park station frequently in the coming months as they continue their investigation into the disappearance of Gus Lamont.

items.title: One Nation circles for frustrated Farrer votes ahead of by-election
items.description: This southern New South Wales town of Gerogery is typically dead on a Monday night, but that all changed when One Nation came to town.

items.title: South West Aboriginal Medical Service slammed in Federal Court
items.description: A federal court judge has found that two board members factionally controlled a South West Indigenous Medical Service and unfairly expelled members to avoid scrutiny and maintain control.
